clips.send: Temperature. A measure of how hot or cold something is. At a higher temperature, particles generally move more vigorously. Even particles in a solid keep vibrating. Internal energy (nèinéng). Add the energy from particles’ motion to the potential energy from their interactions to get the object’s internal energy. Internal energy depends on factors such as temperature, mass, and state. Ice has internal energy, too. Heat (rèliàng). Energy transferred because of a temperature difference, measured in joules (J). The net transfer by heat is from higher to lower temperature. Molecules are always moving randomly. During diffusion (kuòsàn, 扩散), particles move in all directions, with an overall spread from higher to lower concentration. They keep moving after the gases are mixed. Molecules also exert forces on one another. At very close range they repel, and at somewhat greater distances attraction can hold them together.

clips.send: 海水的比热容比许多陆地材料大。暖季海洋吸收大量能量，升温较慢；冷季海洋释放能量，降温也较慢。风把受海洋影响的空气带到陆地时，沿海地区的气温变化往往较小。洋流和风向也会影响这种调节作用。
